newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany posts 7.2 bln DM trade surplus in December. [CORRECTED 08:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Germany posts 7.2 bln DM trade surplus in December. [CORRECTED 08:40 GMT]

text.p: Germany posted a 7.2 billion mark trade surplus in December, down from 9.8 billion marks in November but up from 6.4 billion marks in December 1995, the Federal Statistics Office said on Tuesday.
For 1996, the surplus rose to 97.6 billion marks from 85.3 billion in 1995.

The current account, which includes services as well as visible trade, showed a 3.0 billion mark deficit in December, swinging from a 0.4 billion mark surplus in November, but narrower than a 4.6 billion mark deficit in December 1995.
For 1995, the current-account deficit narrowed to 26.6 billion marks from 29.9 billion marks the previous year.
Exports in December totaled 66 billion marks, down from 70.6 billion marks in November but up from 63.4 billion marks in December 1995.
Imports in the month were 58.8 billion marks, down from 60.8 billion marks in November but up from 57 billion marks in the year-earlier month.
Exports for the full year totaled 784.3 billion marks, up from 749.5 billion marks, while imports rose to 686.7 billion marks from 664.2 billion marks.
